title: DungeonQuest - new expansions coming!
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Fs8L9V90RDk

Daniel (@dungeondive) returns to DungeonQuest, this time the Fantasy Flight revised edition he considers the best version to play, to try three fan-made expansions built by a Dungeon Dive viewer and sold through an Etsy shop: an Events deck, an Undead Merchant, and the Haunted Halls. He rates them among the best fan expansions he has seen.

The Events deck adds a random card each turn (he draws every other, when the sun reaches the top row): dark whispers that demand a luck test, a goblin healer trading determination tokens for wounds, a flood, a possession that sends failures down to the catacombs. The Undead Merchant can be summoned in place of a search and offers three wares for your loot, among them the Keeper's Kiss, a 2400-gold trinket that lifts every attribute and punishes anyone standing next to you. Haunted Halls lets dead heroes return as spirits that stalk the living along the corridors, and Daniel has already adapted it solo as a Jaws-like pursuer.

Brother Gherinn's demonstration game is a catalogue of misfortune. He falls through a bridge into the catacombs, meets a naga, is nearly possessed, walks into the same spear trap twice for ten wounds of thirteen, finds the door jammed twice more, dispels the spirit at his shoulder with one roll, and finally opens the door onto a portcullis his strength of three cannot lift. Daniel adores it, and wishes someone would reprint the game before prices climb further.

----

Fan-made decks are keeping a long out-of-print DungeonQuest alive. Which other game in your collection has been rescued or improved by an unofficial expansion?
